decisions.decision: The 'Preview with a sample partner' path must drive the real SyncService protocol on a delay timer, not a hardcoded pre-completed card.
decisions.rationale: Offline-only build must still genuinely exercise the gated-reveal state machine, including races (both answer same second, edit-after-submit, kill mid-submit); a faked shortcut would make the core invariant untested.
rejected_alternatives: Hardcoded 'already complete' sample card for demo purposes
constraints: Sample partner answers arrive via a timer through LocalSyncService, not a static fixture

decisions.decision: The DesignSystem.swift no-inline-color/font rule is enforced by an automated lint/grep gate, not by code review discretion.
decisions.rationale: An unenforced style promise rots as velocity increases; the gate must be a checkable, running artifact.
rejected_alternatives: Rely on PR review to catch violations
constraints: A script/lint rule scanning for inline Color()/UIColor()/.font(.system(size:)) must exist and run

decisions.decision: Amber is restricted strictly to the tether arc, the two glowing endpoints, and the single 'light the tether' primary action — nowhere else in the UI.
decisions.rationale: Amber is the one accent; without a bright-line rule it creeps onto streak badges, tabs, sliders, CTAs and dilutes the premium feel.
rejected_alternatives: Allow amber on secondary emphasis elements like streak flames or record badges
constraints: Any later-phase amber usage outside these three elements is a violation to flag, not a judgment call

decisions.decision: Card.date / 'today' is anchored to a canonical UTC day boundary computed at the Connection level, never to either individual's local calendar day.
decisions.rationale: The two people are by definition in different timezones; local-day anchoring creates ambiguity about whose midnight defines 'today's card' and is exactly where long-distance apps break.
rejected_alternatives: Anchor to Person A's local day
Anchor to whichever person opens the app first each day
constraints: All day-boundary logic (prompt issuance, streak evaluation) must reference this canonical boundary

decisions.decision: A missed calendar day resets the streak counter to 0 the following day, and this rule must be visibly surfaced in the UI (e.g., Timeline or streak badge), not silently applied.
decisions.rationale: Streaks are a stated success/retention mechanic; silent resets would confuse users and can't be verified without a visible rule.
rejected_alternatives: Silent streak reset with no UI indication
Grace-period streak freeze
constraints: Streak-break state must be discoverable somewhere in the UI

decisions.decision: Tether+ entitlement is modeled on the Connection record, not the Person record, in this local-first build; the simulated partner inherits it automatically.
decisions.rationale: The prompt states billing is 'to one person for the pair' but the data model has no cross-account entitlement concept; scoping entitlement to Connection is the simplest offline-correct approximation.
rejected_alternatives: Model entitlement per-Person and require both to independently subscribe
Defer entitlement modeling entirely to production
constraints: This is flagged as a simplification; the production Firebase-style adapter must revisit real cross-account entitlement sharing — not resolved by this build

decisions.decision: A free user who ends up with more than one connection (e.g., after a Tether+ lapse) never loses data: new-connection creation is blocked, and all non-primary connections become read-only until re-subscribed.
decisions.rationale: The prompt doesn't specify downgrade behavior; silent data loss is unacceptable and must be ruled out explicitly now rather than invented ad hoc by a later phase.
rejected_alternatives: Delete or hide extra connections on downgrade
Leave downgrade behavior undefined
constraints: No destructive deletion of Connection/Card data on entitlement lapse

decisions.decision: CoreMotion-driven globe parallax must degrade gracefully to a static/neutral angle with no crash when device motion is unavailable, which is the default in Simulator.
decisions.rationale: The entire build is staked on being traversable in Simulator offline; an unguarded CoreMotion dependency would crash the very environment the gates run in.
rejected_alternatives: Require a physical device for full gate verification
constraints: Missing CMDeviceMotion must no-op, not throw or crash

decisions.decision: The two-beat heartbeat haptic requirement is scoped, for this offline build, to firing when the simulated partner's timed answer lands while the app is foregrounded — not to background/push-triggered delivery.
decisions.rationale: There is no real second device in local-first testing, so background-push-triggered haptics are untestable here and belong to the production sync-seam scope, not this build's gates.
rejected_alternatives: Treat background push haptic as a testable requirement for this phase
constraints: Background/push haptic behavior is explicitly deferred to the production Firebase-style adapter

decisions.decision: Design and default copy target long-distance couples as the primary audience, while keeping the underlying mechanic and neutral labels (e.g., 'your person') usable for other relationship types.
decisions.rationale: The visual/verbal language in the prompt (tether, ignite, minting ritual) reads romantic-coded even though the prompt explicitly widens scope to friends/family; naming this now prevents copy from silently drifting toward 'partner'-only language.
rejected_alternatives: Design tone equally for all relationship types with no primary framing
Force romantic framing exclusively and drop the broader relationship-type claim from the prompt
constraints: Default onboarding and system copy must never hardcode 'partner' as the label for the other person; keep 'your person' or equivalent neutral phrasing

decisions.decision: Home Screen widget / Lock Screen / Live Activity support is explicitly deferred to V1.1 and stays out of this build's scope.
decisions.rationale: WidgetKit adds real complexity (timeline providers, shared app-group storage, a second design-system render target) that isn't justified for the local-first V1, but it's the single most natural retention mechanic for a once-a-day ritual app and should be named now rather than silently dropped.
rejected_alternatives: Add a basic widget to V1 given how central it is to the retention story
constraints: Do not add WidgetKit targets in this build; flag it as the natural next-version feature in any roadmap output

decisions.decision: 'Preview with a sample partner' is treated as dual-purpose: both the QA/crawler scaffold required by the build contract and the realistic pre-invite persuasion screen a real user would want before sending their join link.
decisions.rationale: The paired-app cold-start problem means the first installer gets no value until their invitee joins; showing them a realistic preview before they commit to inviting someone is the honest product answer within an offline-only build.
rejected_alternatives: Treat sample-partner mode purely as internal test scaffolding with no product-facing framing
constraints: UI copy/design phases should consider surfacing this path as an explicit 'see what you're inviting them into' option, not just a hidden debug/test entry point

decisions.decision: Prompt-list exhaustion (the bundled 60-day list running out) is flagged as an open question for a later content-focused phase rather than solved or ignored in this phase.
decisions.rationale: The prompt doesn't specify post-day-60 behavior; a thin app that goes silent or breaks after 60 days undermines the daily-ritual premise, but solving it now is out of scope for research.
rejected_alternatives: Silently assume infinite unique prompts exist
Solve prompt rotation logic in this phase
constraints: A later phase (design or build) must give an explicit answer, minimally: repeat prompts with a 'you've answered this before' indicator

decisions.decision: The gated-reveal state machine's test suite must use deterministic seeded fixtures (fixed simulated-partner delay timing, fixed prompt id) rather than real timers/randomness.
decisions.rationale: This state machine is the app's core correctness invariant per the prompt contract; non-deterministic test timing risks flaky tests that mask real regressions.
rejected_alternatives: Allow real-time delays and randomized prompt selection in tests for realism
constraints: Build/test phases must seed simulated-partner delay and prompt selection for deterministic, repeatable test runs

decisions.decision: Tether is built as a single app, not split into a portfolio of sibling projects.
decisions.rationale: The prompt is explicitly scoped to one hero surface (the daily distance card); every named screen (onboarding, today, answer sheet, compose & share, timeline, reunion, connections & settings, paywall) is a facet of that one card, not a distinct product. No explicit multi-app or per-category count was requested.
rejected_alternatives: Split into sibling apps by relationship type (couples vs. friends/family)
Split Reunion/Timeline into standalone companion apps
constraints: No portfolio-json manifest is produced
Single Xcode project/target, single DesignSystem.swift, single SyncService seam
No WidgetKit/watchOS companion targets in this build (already deferred to V1.1)

decisions.decision: The selected single app is slug 'tether', category long-distance relationship/daily ritual, target user long-distance couples primarily with relationship-neutral mechanic/copy, build=true.
decisions.rationale: Matches the original prompt and carries forward the product_research audience framing without hardcoding romantic-only language.
constraints: Default copy must keep 'your person' neutral phrasing, never default to 'your partner'

decisions.decision: Settings/Connections screen stays minimal — notification cadence, units, subscription, sign-out only — and no screen beyond the eight named in the prompt contract gets built.
decisions.rationale: Guards against shell-padding scope creep (extra stats screens, settings sprawl) on a build already carrying 19 hard requirements plus StoreKit/CoreMotion/AVAssetWriter/design-lint work.
rejected_alternatives: Allow later phases to add convenience screens as needed
constraints: Any new screen proposed later must justify itself against 'does it make the card more beautiful, emotional, or shareable'

decisions.decision: Lock the one-sentence product promise: Tether is a daily two-sided distance card that only completes when both people answer.
decisions.rationale: Gives every later phase a single, unambiguous test for scope creep — if a feature doesn't serve this gated-reveal moment, it's out.
rejected_alternatives: Describing Tether as a broader long-distance relationship toolkit/super-app
constraints: Later phases must be able to explain the app in this one sentence

decisions.decision: The Answer sheet is the only free-text entry surface in the entire app.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the app from creeping toward messaging/chat, which is explicitly out of scope.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing comments or free text elsewhere (e.g. on Timeline cards)
constraints: No text input control may be added outside the Answer sheet in any future phase

decisions.decision: Once both answers exist and a card is complete, both answers are final and uneditable, and this finality must be visibly communicated at submission time.
decisions.rationale: Avoids an ambiguous 'can I edit after they've seen it' state that would otherwise be discovered as a bug later; matches the two-sided gated-reveal being the emotional core of the app.
rejected_alternatives: Allow silent post-reveal edits
Allow edits only before the other person has answered, with no UI signal of the cutoff
constraints: UI must make answer finality legible at the moment of submission, not just disable an edit control invisibly

decisions.decision: The Today screen's very first rendered frame must truthfully convey card state (waiting-on-them / waiting-on-you / complete) with zero required taps and before any animation completes.
decisions.rationale: This is a daily-use ritual app; users open it specifically to check status, and Reduce Motion users need the same information without relying on animation.
rejected_alternatives: Requiring the full draw-on/reveal animation to finish before state is legible
constraints: Motion/design phases must treat first-frame legibility as a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have

decisions.decision: Adopt four concrete, checkable success criteria for this build: full offline traversability of all eight screens via sample-partner mode, deterministic race-condition test coverage of the gated-reveal state machine, zero non-sanctioned amber pixels verified by lint, and instant truthful state legibility on Today's first frame.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires measurable success criteria, not vibes; these four are each independently verifiable by a script or test rather than subjective review.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving success criteria as qualitative/descriptive only
constraints: Build-verification phases should check against these four criteria explicitly

decisions.decision: After the bundled 60-day prompt list is exhausted, the schedule repeats from day 1, with a small badge on the prompt indicating 'you've answered this before — has anything changed?'
decisions.rationale: A daily-ritual app cannot go silent or repeat unlabeled after two months; this is a correctness requirement, not a content nice-to-have, and doubles as a low-cost emotional callback feature (comparing today's answer to a year-ago answer).
rejected_alternatives: Leaving post-day-60 behavior undefined
Silently repeating prompts with no indication they've been seen before
constraints: Prompt-repeat logic and the 'answered before' badge must be implemented as part of the daily prompt issuance flow, not deferred further

decisions.decision: Until a connection is actually joined by the invited partner, the Today screen defaults to the clearly-labeled 'Preview with a sample partner' experience (one tap to dismiss into an explicit 'waiting for [name] to join' state), rather than an empty/spinner state.
decisions.rationale: The cold-start gap between install and partner-join is the single most fragile retention window this product has and is outside the product's control to shorten; showing a labeled preview keeps the app alive rather than dead during that gap.
rejected_alternatives: Showing a bare empty state or spinner until the partner joins
constraints: This makes 'Preview with a sample partner' a shipped product surface with real default-visibility, not just a hidden QA/debug entry point, extending DEC-product_research-003

decisions.decision: The full tether draw-on/minting animation (~1.1s) plays only on first pairing and on card completion; on ordinary app reopens, the Today screen's first frame is instantly state-legible with no animation delay.
decisions.rationale: A daily-use app reopened many times a day cannot force a 1.1s animation on every visit without damaging retention; the ritual animation belongs to genuinely special moments, not routine status checks.
rejected_alternatives: Replaying the full draw-on animation on every app open
constraints: Resolves the open risk carried from initial_discussion; motion/design phases must implement 'reopen' as a distinct, instantly-legible state from 'first pairing' and 'completion'

decisions.decision: Lock the exact free vs. Tether+ value split: free tier delivers the complete emotional loop (pairing, globe, daily prompt, gated reveal, streak, Timeline, one static export/day); Tether+ unlocks animated export, additional connections, premium skins, and the Reunion module plus annual Year Tethered retrospective — genuine capability differences, not cosmetic gating.
decisions.rationale: Matches the prompt_contract monetization spec exactly and satisfies this phase's acceptance check that subscription value be functional, not cosmetic.
rejected_alternatives: Gating any part of the core daily card loop behind Tether+
constraints: No future phase may move any part of the daily card loop behind the paywall

decisions.decision: The competitive wedge is defined as uncompromising craft on a single moment (the two-sided gated reveal) combined with a structurally-forced invite growth mechanic (a card cannot be created solo, so K≥1 by construction); no future feature may introduce a way to use Tether solo.
decisions.rationale: This is what differentiates Tether from commodity distance-counter apps and from messaging-heavy paired apps like Between; the forced-invite mechanic is rare and must be protected as a hard constraint, not a soft preference.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing an eventual solo/single-user mode for convenience
constraints: Any later phase proposing solo card creation or optional pairing must be rejected outright

decisions.decision: The documented Firebase-style SyncService adapter is the designated production target, not a stretch goal — it is the only path to real background-push heartbeat haptics and honest per-person/cross-account Tether+ entitlement, both of which the local-first build explicitly cannot deliver.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the brief honest that the local build is a complete, shippable v1 but not a permanent feature ceiling; prevents a later phase from treating the Connection-scoped entitlement simplification as a final design decision.
rejected_alternatives: Treating cloud sync as optional/future polish with no explicit commitment
constraints: Any roadmap output must state cloud adapter work as the defined next step, not an open-ended maybe

decisions.decision: The MVP slice is the full core loop end-to-end, including real onboarding/pairing via the sample-partner path and city search — not a stripped, hardcoded pre-paired mock.
decisions.rationale: Pairing is the locked, non-negotiable structurally-forced growth mechanic, and 'Preview with a sample partner' was already decided to be a dual-purpose, load-bearing product screen (QA scaffold + pre-invite persuasion), not omittable scaffolding; cutting it would validate a generic globe/reveal tech demo instead of this app's actual concept.
rejected_alternatives: Gemini's proposal to launch directly into a hardcoded pre-paired mock relationship, cutting onboarding, pairing, invite-code generation, and city search from this slice to focus purely on globe-rendering and state-machine engineering risk
constraints: The later build phase must implement the full slice described here, not a thinned demo version

decisions.decision: This slice explicitly defers (not deletes): animated MP4/Live Photo export (ship static PNG-with-watermark only), premium skins beyond classic indigo (architect the extension point, populate one), the Reunion module and Year Tethered retrospective, multi-connection management, and fine parallax tuning beyond the required static fallback.
decisions.rationale: Sequences the riskiest native-media code (AVAssetWriter) and secondary emotional payoffs after the core daily-card loop has proven itself, per this phase's goal of the smallest slice that proves the concept.
rejected_alternatives: Cutting into globe fidelity, gated-reveal correctness, or the signature haptics to save build time
constraints: The skin/export architecture must still exist as a real extension point so later phases aren't rewrites, even though only one skin and no animated export ship in this slice

decisions.decision: Adopt two additional technical validation requirements raised by the skeptic pass: coastline-polyline globe rendering must not stutter in the Simulator with CoreMotion parallax active, and the gated-reveal state machine must have explicit test coverage for the simulated partner's timer firing while the Answer sheet is open/mid-edit.
decisions.rationale: These are two concrete, previously-unnamed failure modes that are cheap to specify now and expensive to discover late, given the state machine is already locked as the app's core correctness invariant.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving globe performance and this specific race condition unspecified, relying on general test coverage language from earlier phases
constraints: Build/test phases must add both as explicit, checkable test cases, not just general performance/race awareness

decisions.decision: Lock five validation criteria for this slice: full offline zero-state-to-archived-card traversal with no placeholders, deterministic seeded state-machine coverage including the newly named timer/keyboard race, zero-tap truthful first-frame legibility on Today, zero non-sanctioned amber pixels via lint, and stutter-free globe rendering under parallax.
decisions.rationale: Gives the build-verification phase concrete, independently-checkable pass/fail criteria rather than a qualitative description of the slice.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving validation criteria qualitative/descriptive only
constraints: Build-verification phases should check against these five criteria explicitly, in addition to the four already adopted in initial_discussion

decisions.decision: Sample-partner mode data (cards, streak, Timeline) lives on a separate, disposable Connection that is discarded — not merged — the moment a real partner joins, and that transition gets its own distinct visible beat.
decisions.rationale: Sample-partner mode is now a shipped, default-visible product surface, so a real user could accumulate days of fake activity against it; silently merging that into the real Connection once a partner joins would be a data-integrity bug baked into the product's own design.
rejected_alternatives: Merging sample-partner cards/streak into the real Connection once a partner joins
Silently swapping the underlying data with no visible transition moment
constraints: Build phase must model the sample-partner Connection as a distinct, clearly-flagged entity that does not persist forward into the real pairing

decisions.decision: The join-link/code share action is honest that it generates a real link string, but onboarding UI must make explicit that experiencing the paired state in this offline build is only possible via 'Preview with a sample partner' — never implying working peer-to-peer invite delivery.
decisions.rationale: This build has no networking, so a share sheet that appears to send an invite with no possible receipt on the other end is a dishonest affordance, not just a limitation.
rejected_alternatives: Letting onboarding copy/UI imply that sending the join link actually delivers a working invite in this build
constraints: Onboarding copy phase must state this scoping explicitly

decisions.decision: Streak UI must visibly distinguish 'your personal answer streak' from 'the connection's completion streak,' and a broken completion streak must legibly communicate whether the break was caused by the user or by their partner not answering.
decisions.rationale: Only completed cards extend the streak, so a user who answers faithfully every day can still see their streak hit zero because their partner went quiet; an opaque single number reads as the app punishing the wrong person.
rejected_alternatives: Showing only a single aggregate streak number with no attribution of why it reset
constraints: Timeline/streak badge design must carry per-person answered-state, not just the aggregate streak count

decisions.decision: 'Primary connection' for the free-tier downgrade rule (DEC-prompt_contract-007) is deterministically defined as the earliest-created Connection; every connection created after it becomes read-only on a Tether+ lapse.
decisions.rationale: The existing downgrade rule is unimplementable without a deterministic tiebreaker; earliest-created matches the free tier's own 'one connection' framing.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'primary' undefined for a later phase to invent ad hoc
Making primary user-selectable, which adds unrequested complexity
constraints: Build phase must implement this exact ordering rule

decisions.decision: The build must include a way to simulate an expired/lapsed Tether+ subscription against the bundled .storekit config (StoreKit Testing supports simulating renewal failure/expiration) so the downgrade/read-only rule is actually exercised by a test, not just specified on paper.
decisions.rationale: An untested downgrade rule is unverified; StoreKit Testing natively supports simulating this scenario, so there's no excuse to leave it unexercised.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the downgrade/read-only path unverified in offline gates
constraints: Test suite must include a lapsed-entitlement scenario exercising the read-only-connection behavior

decisions.decision: It is an accepted, explicitly named limitation that if the simulated partner's answer timer fires while the app is backgrounded, the user feels no heartbeat haptic and simply finds the card already complete on return.
decisions.rationale: This follows directly from the already-locked foreground-only haptic scoping (DEC-prompt_contract-009); naming it now prevents it from being discovered later as an unexplained bug.
rejected_alternatives: Building a foreground-return catch-up haptic to simulate a felt moment retroactively
constraints: No new feature required; documented as a known limitation only

decisions.decision: If a SwiftData save fails when submitting an answer, the Answer sheet retains the typed draft and shows a retry/error state rather than silently discarding the user's input.
decisions.rationale: The Answer sheet is the only free-text entry surface in the entire app, so silently losing that one input is a much higher-stakes failure than in an app with redundant entry points.
rejected_alternatives: Silently dropping the draft on a save failure
constraints: Answer sheet must implement an explicit error/retry UI state

decisions.decision: The one-line answer has an explicit, enforced character cap rather than 'one line' being merely a design intention.
decisions.rationale: The card is a fixed hero layout; without an enforced input-level cap, an unusually long answer is a layout bug waiting to happen.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on visual wrapping/truncation with no input-level enforcement
constraints: Design/build phase must pick and enforce a specific maximum character count

decisions.decision: The hand-drawn Canvas globe must expose an explicit accessibility label/value summarizing card and distance state (e.g. 'You are 2,847 km from [name]. Card complete.') for VoiceOver.
decisions.rationale: A fully custom-drawn Canvas view has zero default accessibility elements; per the global rule that accessibility is a product requirement, not polish, this needs an explicit fix.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the globe as a purely visual, VoiceOver-invisible element
constraints: Build phase must attach an accessibility summary to the globe view

decisions.decision: The Settings notification-cadence control must not imply working push notifications in this offline build — its copy is either explicitly scoped to foreground/in-app alerts only, or the control is disabled with an honest explanation.
decisions.rationale: Per DEC-prompt_contract-009, background/push delivery is out of scope for this build; an unscoped toggle that quietly does nothing would be a dishonest affordance.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping a notification-cadence toggle with no functional effect and no explanatory copy
constraints: Settings screen copy must state this scoping explicitly

decisions.decision: Lock three final build assumptions: the app is English-only/unlocalized with a functional but untranslated km/mi toggle; device-clock manipulation to fake streaks or force a Reunion countdown to zero is an accepted, low-priority risk not defended against in v1; and home location is stored/displayed at city-level precision only (never GPS-precise or continuously tracked), disclosed plainly in onboarding copy.
decisions.rationale: Converts three previously-unaddressed open questions into explicit, scoped assumptions rather than leaving them for a later phase to discover or resolve inconsistently.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving localization, clock-tampering defense, and location-precision disclosure unaddressed
constraints: Onboarding copy must include the city-level-precision disclosure
No anti-tampering/clock-defense engineering work is in scope for v1

decisions.decision: Add a distinct 'redeem your own join code on a second simulated identity' affordance, separate from 'Preview with a sample partner,' as the only mechanism that triggers the sample-data-discard transition.
decisions.rationale: DEC-detailed_discussion-001 requires discarding sample-partner data 'the moment a real partner joins,' but DEC-detailed_discussion-002 already established this offline build has no networking and can never receive a real invite — without this affordance, the discard/transition requirement is unimplementable and untestable.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the sample-to-real transition as an unimplementable rule on paper
Overloading 'Preview with a sample partner' itself as the trigger, conflating persuasion-preview and real-pairing-simulation into one ambiguous mode
constraints: This affordance must be clearly labeled as distinct from sample-partner preview mode
Its sole purpose is enabling a real, testable 'partner joined' transition

decisions.decision: The bare capability to create a second Connection when Tether+-entitled is must-have in this build, even though full Connections list management/reordering stays deferred.
decisions.rationale: DEC-detailed_discussion-005 requires the free-tier downgrade/read-only rule to be exercised by a real StoreKit-Testing-simulated lapse, but that is impossible without first being able to create a second connection, which DEC-next_steps_small-002 had deferred entirely — the two decisions were in direct tension.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving multi-connection creation fully deferred and treating the downgrade rule as unverified in this build
constraints: Only a bare 'add connection' action is required, not a polished management UI
This exists solely to make the downgrade/read-only rule testable

decisions.decision: Split Reunion into a must-have reachable screen with correct paywall-gating for free users, and a should-have real countdown for entitled users; the Year Tethered retrospective reel stays won't-build.
decisions.rationale: Reunion is one of the eight named screens, and 'all eight screens reachable' is a locked success criterion (DEC-initial_discussion-005); bucketing all of Reunion into deferred would silently violate that criterion, but the full retrospective reel is genuinely expensive and not needed to satisfy reachability/paywall correctness.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring Reunion entirely as part of the same lump as the Year Tethered reel
constraints: Reunion screen + its paywall trigger is must-have; real countdown is should-have; retrospective reel remains won't-build

decisions.decision: The animated-export toggle remains visible in Compose & Share for correct paywall-gating, but resolves to an explicit 'coming soon' state for entitled Tether+ users rather than crashing, silently no-opping, or faking a file.
decisions.rationale: Since StoreKit purchases must genuinely succeed in this build for entitlement testing, a real entitled user could reach this toggle and hit a dead end; an honest 'coming soon' state avoids a dishonest or broken-looking affordance while still deferring the actual AVAssetWriter work.
rejected_alternatives: Hiding the toggle entirely for entitled users (breaks demonstrable paywall-gating for free users)
Letting the toggle silently no-op or crash for entitled users
constraints: No AVAssetWriter/animated export work is implemented in this build

decisions.decision: Locked concrete, individually testable acceptance criteria replacing vague prior phrasing: first-frame legibility as a pure Card→CardDisplayState unit test; globe performance as vertex-count budget + throttled parallax updates rather than an automated perf gate; CoreMotion degradation and Reduce Motion each as dedicated unit tests; the three named races as three distinct seeded-fixture tests; the design-lint gate as an actual failing script; and the downgrade rule as one explicit end-to-end StoreKit-Testing scenario.
decisions.rationale: Several previously-locked requirements (globe doesn't stutter, first-frame is legible, race coverage exists) were specified qualitatively enough that a build phase could satisfy them with weak or unverifiable tests; this phase converts each into something an adherence gate can actually check.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these requirements as qualitative descriptions for the build phase to interpret
Promising an automated Simulator performance gate that can't reliably be built
constraints: Build-verification must check each of these as a discrete, named test, not a general performance/race awareness claim

decisions.decision: Name the design language 'Night Instrument Panel': a dark console aesthetic where amber is rationed to the tether/endpoints/primary action and everything else reads in desaturated ivory-on-indigo, including all navigation chrome.
decisions.rationale: Directly extends already-locked constraints (amber restricted to three elements, a separate monospaced 'instrument' type voice) into a coherent, app-specific visual identity rather than a generic 'clean and modern' non-answer.
rejected_alternatives: A diary/journal-coded aesthetic
A generic romance-coded visual language
constraints: All future screen/component design must read as 'instrument panel', not app-chrome-with-accent-color

decisions.decision: Lock the emotional target: the user should feel the quiet, held-breath anticipation of checking a shared vital sign, resolving into a small real thrill when the card completes — explicitly not a feed-scroll dopamine feeling.
decisions.rationale: Gives later design/motion/copy phases a concrete emotional bar to design toward rather than leaving tone undefined.
rejected_alternatives: Designing for generic 'delight' or feed-like engagement
constraints: Motion, haptics, and copy phases should be checked against this one-sentence target

decisions.decision: The signature interaction is the gated reveal expressed as persistent visual grammar (a visibly dim/thin tether with one dashed-placeholder answer slot before completion, versus a glowing/taut tether with both answers cross-dissolved in after completion) — not just a one-time animation.
decisions.rationale: Card state must be legible from static layout alone given the already-locked requirement that reopens are instantly state-legible with no animation replay; a purely motion-based signature interaction would fail that requirement on ordinary reopens.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the ~1.1s draw-on animation itself as the sole signature interaction with no persistent half-lit visual state
constraints: Build phase must implement a distinct 'half-lit/dim-thin tether' visual state, not just an animation timeline

decisions.decision: Reject the stock TabView/List/system-tint default explicitly: no bottom tab bar (Today is the chrome-free root; Timeline/Reunion/Settings are small corner affordances on Today), zero system tint anywhere outside the three sanctioned amber uses, Timeline renders as stacked miniature hero cards rather than List rows, and the instrument monospaced type family is reserved exclusively for clock/distance/coordinates.
decisions.rationale: Concrete, named differences are required by this phase rather than vague adjectives; each difference is directly justified by an already-locked constraint (amber rationing, instrument type voice, narrow eight-screen surface).
rejected_alternatives: A standard TabView-based navigation shell with system accent color and List-row Timeline
constraints: No bottom tab bar in the default build; no system tint color used anywhere outside the three sanctioned amber elements

decisions.decision: Corner-icon navigation to Timeline/Reunion/Settings is accepted as the default, but is an explicit discoverability bet: if a new user cannot find all three within a couple of taps, the fallback is a minimal, still-desaturated tab bar rather than shipping an app that feels smaller than its real screen count.
decisions.rationale: Ties an unconventional navigation choice to a concrete, checkable usability bar instead of asserting it works by design intuition alone.
rejected_alternatives: Committing to corner-icon navigation unconditionally with no discoverability check or fallback plan
constraints: Build/verification phases should informally check first-time discoverability of Timeline/Reunion/Settings before treating corner-icon navigation as final

decisions.decision: Locked/premium/'coming soon' UI states (locked skins, the animated-export toggle) use a neutral dimmed/lock-glyph treatment and must never use amber.
decisions.rationale: Extends the existing hard rule that amber is restricted to exactly three elements with a concrete corollary the build phase could otherwise get wrong by reaching for amber as a natural 'this is special/premium' signal.
rejected_alternatives: Using amber or a variant of it to indicate premium/locked content
constraints: Design-lint/amber audits must treat locked/coming-soon indicators as a checked case, not just the three sanctioned elements

decisions.decision: Lock a full per-screen state inventory: onboarding's three visually distinct entry actions (name+code generation, soft sample-partner preview, redeem-code with a confirmation beat since it irreversibly discards sample data); Today's five states (awaiting-you, awaiting-them, complete, streak-broken-and-attributed, sample-partner-waiting); Answer sheet's four states (empty, typing-with-counter, error-retry, locked-after-completion); Compose & Share's locked-skin/coming-soon states; Timeline's designed empty state; Reunion's four states (free-gated, entitled-no-date, active-countdown, milestone-zero); Settings' visually distinct read-only-vs-active subscription row; Paywall's contextual entry copy plus purchase-in-progress/success/error.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires real screens/states, not vague UX language; this converts every screen into an implementable state machine a SwiftUI developer can build directly from.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving screen states as qualitative descriptions for the build phase to invent
constraints: Build phase must implement each named state explicitly, not merge them into a single generic view

decisions.decision: The redeem-join-code action (which triggers irreversible discard of sample-partner data per DEC-app_features-001) must present a confirmation beat before executing, not a bare tap-through.
decisions.rationale: This is the one action in onboarding with a permanent, irreversible side effect (discarding sample data); a silent tap-through risks accidental data loss the user didn't intend.
rejected_alternatives: Executing the redeem-code discard transition on a single unconfirmed tap
constraints: Build phase must add an explicit confirmation step to the redeem-code flow

decisions.decision: An explicit fallback (either a controlled minimum font-size floor while other text keeps scaling, or allowing the readout to wrap to two lines) must be decided for the instrument-type hero distance readout and dual clock at the largest Dynamic Type accessibility sizes, where the compressed/tightly-tracked font risks clipping or overflow.
decisions.rationale: Dynamic Type scaling is already a hard requirement, but no prior phase specified what the ~80pt hero readout and dual clock actually do at maximum accessibility text sizes; without an explicit rule this becomes a layout bug discovered late rather than a decided design behavior.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the hero readout's behavior at maximum Dynamic Type sizes unspecified
constraints: Build phase must pick and implement one explicit fallback strategy for the display/meta type styles at accessibility sizes

decisions.decision: Tether supports both a real light appearance and a real dark (default/primary) appearance with explicit hex values for every semantic color role, rather than forcing dark-only via .preferredColorScheme(.dark).
decisions.rationale: The phase's own acceptance check requires every color role to have both a light and dark hex value, and the global build rule requires both appearances to be verified; the original prompt says 'dark-first' not 'dark-only', so dark stays the primary designed experience while light remains a fully defined, non-stub appearance.
rejected_alternatives: Forcing .preferredColorScheme(.dark) app-wide and shipping only one appearance
constraints: Every DesignSystem color token must carry both a light and dark hex value
Build-verification must check both appearances, not just dark

decisions.decision: The Dynamic Type accessibility-size fallback is resolved per-component: the Display distance readout uses a clamped minimum size (54pt floor) with minimumScaleFactor(0.74) and stays single-line; the DualClockRow instead adaptively stacks the two clocks vertically past the .accessibility1 category rather than wrapping.
decisions.rationale: Finalizes the open question from DEC-design_discussion-009 by applying each of the two proposed strategies to the component it actually fits: a single continuous numeral ('2,847 km') breaks visually if wrapped mid-unit, while two independent clock values can cleanly restack.
rejected_alternatives: Applying one single strategy (either clamp-only or wrap-only) to both the Display readout and the dual clock
constraints: Build phase must implement Display with a hard 54pt/0.74 floor, single-line only
Build phase must implement DualClockRow with a vertical-stack breakpoint, not text wrapping

decisions.decision: No external Claude Design pass is used; this phase's DESIGN SPEC plus the resulting Theme.swift is the complete, direct handoff to the build phase.
decisions.rationale: The spec is already fully numeric (exact hex, point sizes, spacing, radii, a hand-specified Canvas signature element, a three-color lint rule); importing an externally generated mockup risks reintroducing arbitrary colors/fonts that the lint gate would then have to fight.
rejected_alternatives: Using the drafted Claude Design prompt to generate an external mockup for import
constraints: Build phase proceeds directly from this document, no external design import step

decisions.decision: Lock the full canonical design-token spec (type scale, 8pt spacing grid, semantic color palette including a new bgElevated sheet tier, corner radii, component inventory, navigation/sheet map, per-screen states, motion/haptics, accessibility) synthesizing both contributors' input into one non-conflicting source of truth.
decisions.rationale: Two independently-produced specs this round overlapped heavily but used different exact values in several places (spacing scale, radii, color tokens, type fallback); the build phase needs exactly one authoritative numeric spec, not two to reconcile itself.
rejected_alternatives: Handing the build phase both raw contributions and letting it pick
constraints: Theme.swift must be written from this merged spec, not from either individual contributor's numbers where they conflicted

decisions.decision: Carry forward non-visual architecture guidance as build-phase requirements: an @Observable AppRouter owning activeConnectionID/presentedSheet/onboarding phase; the gated-reveal display logic implemented as a pure, SwiftUI-free Card→CardDisplayState function; CoreMotion attitude throttled into ephemeral view state that never triggers a SwiftData @Query refetch; and the redeem-code action disabled whenever any sheet is presented to prevent an atomic Connection-swap race against an open Answer-sheet draft.
decisions.rationale: These are concrete, previously-unspecified implementation requirements that directly protect already-locked correctness/performance requirements (R-012 first-frame legibility as a pure unit test, the globe-stutter risk named in next_steps_small, and the sample-to-real transition race named in detailed_discussion) rather than being optional style preferences.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these as implicit implementation details for the build phase to invent
constraints: Build phase must implement the gated-reveal display state as a pure function with no SwiftUI import
Build phase must disable the redeem-code action while any sheet is presented

decisions.decision: Adopt a SyncService protocol with LocalSyncService (SwiftData-backed) as the active implementation and a documented, unbuilt FirebaseSyncService as the production adapter.
decisions.rationale: Matches the already-locked production seam requirement while keeping the local build's only real implementation simple and testable.
rejected_alternatives: Building a partial/stubbed cloud adapter now
constraints: FirebaseSyncService remains documentation-only in this build

decisions.decision: The simulated partner's answer timing must be persisted as a due-date on Card and resolved via deterministic checkpoint evaluation (onAppear, scenePhase .active, foreground timer tick) rather than an in-memory sleeping Task/Timer.
decisions.rationale: iOS suspends backgrounded apps; a live sleeping Task will die mid-wait and silently break the already-locked 'no heartbeat if backgrounded, card just appears complete' behavior instead of implementing it correctly.
rejected_alternatives: Task.sleep-based simulated delay running only while foregrounded
Wall-clock Timer scheduled at answer-start with no persisted due-date
constraints: Card model must carry a persisted simulatedPartnerAnswerDueAt (or equivalent structured state)
Completion must be evaluated opportunistically at named checkpoints, not assumed from a running timer

decisions.decision: Structure the domain layer as five explicit service protocols — SyncService, PromptProvider, GlobeDataService, EntitlementService, HapticsService — each with a local default implementation, injected into an @Observable AppRouter that is the sole owner of cross-screen navigation state.
decisions.rationale: Prevents views from independently mutating activeConnectionID/presentedSheet, which is exactly how sheet-presentation and connection-swap races get introduced.
rejected_alternatives: Letting individual views own their own navigation/state transition logic
constraints: No view may mutate AppRouter's core state except through router-owned methods

decisions.decision: The gated-reveal display logic is implemented as a pure, SwiftUI-free function (Card, Connection, now) -> CardDisplayState with an injectable clock for deterministic testing.
decisions.rationale: Extends design_handoff's pure-function requirement with the clock-injection needed to make the state machine and its races testable in milliseconds without flaky real-time waits.
rejected_alternatives: Testing state transitions only via UI/XCUITest with real timers
constraints: Function must accept an injected 'now' rather than calling Date() directly

decisions.decision: SwiftData persistence covers Person, Connection, Card, Prompt, Reunion, and a lightweight AppSettings record; all primary keys are UUIDs; sample-partner data lives on a separate isSample-flagged, disposable Connection row.
decisions.rationale: UUIDs avoid a later migration when reconciling with the documented Firebase-style adapter's client-generated IDs; the isSample Connection row makes the already-locked atomic discard-on-redeem-code transition (DEC-app_features-001, DEC-detailed_discussion-001) a real, testable write rather than an ad hoc flag check.
rejected_alternatives: Auto-incrementing integer IDs
Flagging sample-partner data on the same Connection row as real pairing data
constraints: ModelContainer must be configured with cloudKitDatabase: .none explicitly
SwiftUI Previews use a separate in-memory ModelContainer seeded with fixture data

decisions.decision: No CoreLocation/location permission is used anywhere in the app; home location is selected only from the bundled city seed list.
decisions.rationale: Matches the already-locked city-level-precision-only decision (DEC-detailed_discussion-011); adding CoreLocation for 'faster city search' would be permission scope creep the product explicitly promised not to need.
rejected_alternatives: Using CLLocationManager to suggest a default city
constraints: No location usage-description keys or CoreLocation imports in this build

decisions.decision: No push/UNUserNotificationCenter permission is requested in this build; the Settings notification-cadence control persists a preference value for the future cloud adapter without triggering a system permission prompt, and its copy honestly states it governs foreground/in-app alerts only.
decisions.rationale: There is structurally nothing to notify about in an offline, foreground-only simulated-partner build; requesting a permission for a feature that cannot fire is a dishonest affordance and an avoidable App Review flag.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting notification permission preemptively for future cloud sync
constraints: Extends DEC-detailed_discussion-010's scoped-copy requirement to also mean no permission prompt is triggered

decisions.decision: CoreMotion device-motion (attitude/parallax) usage requires no Info.plist usage-description key, since only CMMotionManager.deviceMotion is used, not CMMotionActivityManager/CMPedometer; the code must still guard isDeviceMotionAvailable and stop updates on backgrounding.
decisions.rationale: This is the technically accurate Apple platform behavior; adding an unused usage-description key for a permission dialog that never appears is confusing rather than a safety margin, and the real risk (crashing/draining battery) is already covered by the availability guard and backgrounding stop.
rejected_alternatives: Adding NSMotionUsageDescription defensively even though it's not required for the APIs actually used
constraints: Must call stopDeviceMotionUpdates on scene backgrounding
Must check isDeviceMotionAvailable before starting updates (already locked by DEC-prompt_contract-008)

decisions.decision: Photos-library-read permission is never requested; export uses ShareLink/share-sheet only in this build, with any future explicit 'Save to Photos' action deferred to when it's actually built, using add-only authorization at that time.
decisions.rationale: The current export scope (static PNG, share sheet) doesn't need Photos access at all; requesting it preemptively would be an unused, unjustifiable permission.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting full or add-only Photos access now for a feature not yet built
constraints: No PHPhotoLibrary imports/usage in this slice

decisions.decision: Entitlement truth is centralized in a single @Observable EntitlementStore backed by StoreKit 2's Transaction.currentEntitlements and Transaction.updates; Connection-scoped business rules (primary connection, read-only lapse behavior) are derived rules layered on top of that one signal, never independently persisted booleans.
decisions.rationale: A boolean cached on the Connection model can drift out of sync with what StoreKit actually grants; centralizing avoids the exact class of bug where UI and entitlement truth disagree.
rejected_alternatives: Persisting an entitlement boolean directly on Connection as the source of truth
constraints: All free/paid gating and downgrade logic must read through EntitlementStore, not a cached field

decisions.decision: The Paywall must include a 'Restore Purchases' action, and the bundled .storekit configuration file must be attached to the shared Xcode scheme so headless xcodebuild test can simulate purchases in CI/gates.
decisions.rationale: Restore Purchases is a real App Store requirement for subscription products, not optional polish; the StoreKit-configuration-must-be-in-the-scheme requirement is a known 'works in Xcode, silently fails headless' trap worth writing down before the build phase hits it blind.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Restore Purchases as a should-have
Leaving StoreKit config scheme-attachment undocumented and discovering the CI failure later
constraints: Scheme → Options → StoreKit Configuration must reference the .storekit file explicitly

decisions.decision: Haptics use UIImpactFeedbackGenerator (.soft/.rigid) and UINotificationFeedbackGenerator, not CoreHaptics; generators are instantiated once and .prepare()'d ahead of the triggering gesture.
decisions.rationale: CoreHaptics is built for custom .ahap pattern authoring; the two documented feedback styles (heartbeat, crisp tick) don't need that complexity or file format.
rejected_alternatives: Authoring custom CoreHaptics patterns for the heartbeat/tick
constraints: Generators must no-op safely on Simulator/hardware without haptics, per already-locked graceful-degradation expectations

decisions.decision: Export uses a CardExporter protocol (export(card:skin:) async throws -> ExportResult) with a single StaticPNGExporter conformer (ImageRenderer-based) shipping now; Compose & Share's animated toggle checks for a registered animated exporter rather than a hardcoded boolean.
decisions.rationale: Makes the already-locked 'coming soon' animated-export state (DEC-app_features-004) and the deferred AVAssetWriter work additive later rather than a refactor of Compose & Share's gating logic.
rejected_alternatives: Hardcoding a boolean 'animated export available' flag that a later phase has to rewire
constraints: Compose & Share must query exporter registration, not a static flag

decisions.decision: Testing splits into a pure-logic unit target (state machine, day boundary, streak attribution, prompt-repeat indexing, and four seeded races) and a thin XCUITest layer limited to one eight-screen sample-partner crawl, plus one StoreKit-Testing entitlement-expiry scenario.
decisions.rationale: Keeps correctness testing fast and deterministic in the pure-logic layer while reserving the flakiest tool (XCUITest) for exactly one job it's suited to: proving all eight screens are reachable and state-legible.
rejected_alternatives: Testing business logic primarily through XCUITest
A single mixed test target with no layering
constraints: The fourth race — redeem-code atomic swap firing while an unresolved simulated-answer due-date is pending on the connection being discarded — must be an explicit seeded test alongside the three already-locked races
All race/timing tests use an injected clock, never real sleeps

decisions.decision: The design-lint gate is a standalone shell/Python script (not a new tool dependency) grepping *.swift outside Theme.swift for inline Color(/UIColor(/.font(.system(size: patterns, run as a CI/gate step.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the already-locked automated-lint requirement (DEC-prompt_contract-002) without introducing a linter package that would itself need a dependency justification.
rejected_alternatives: Adopting a third-party SwiftLint-style tool for this single rule
constraints: Script must run as part of the build-verification gate, not be optional

decisions.decision: The one-line answer character cap is set to 80 characters, enforced at the TextField binding with a hard truncating constraint, not merely a UI counter label.
decisions.rationale: Closes the DEC-detailed_discussion-008 requirement for an enforced (not just displayed) cap with a concrete, reasonable number so tech_specs doesn't stall re-litigating it.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the cap as a soft/visual-only counter
Deferring the exact number to tech_specs
constraints: Enforcement happens at the binding/input layer, not just in submit validation

decisions.decision: Entitlement-gated writes (e.g. answering/creating cards on a non-primary, non-entitled connection) are rejected from a single domain policy point, not only hidden via UI visibility.
decisions.rationale: Gating only at the UI layer leaves the underlying data layer able to silently accept writes it shouldn't, undermining the already-locked no-data-loss downgrade rule (DEC-prompt_contract-007).
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on disabling/hiding UI controls for read-only connections
constraints: All Card/Connection mutation paths must route through this single policy check

decisions.decision: Person, Connection, Card, Prompt, Reunion, and AppSettings are implemented exactly once, as SwiftData @Model classes — not as parallel Codable struct duplicates of the same names returned by a service layer.
decisions.rationale: Two contributors independently defined 'Card'/'Connection' with different kinds (Codable struct vs @Model class) in the same round; parallel build lanes cannot code against two competing definitions of the same entity, and @Model instances can be constructed unattached to a live ModelContext, so pure-function unit tests lose nothing by skipping a separate DTO layer.
rejected_alternatives: Maintaining parallel plain-struct domain types alongside @Model persistence types
constraints: Exactly one type per named domain entity
SyncService methods that return e.g. Card return the @Model instance directly

decisions.decision: Adopt a single CardScene value type (built by buildCardScene) as the one source the live globe draw, the VoiceOver accessibility summary, and the static PNG exporter all read from, rather than each independently re-deriving projection/geometry.
decisions.rationale: Eliminates a whole class of 'the exported card doesn't match what I saw on screen' bugs and duplicate geometry logic across three consumers.
rejected_alternatives: Letting GlobeView, StaticPNGExporter, and the accessibility label each independently call GlobeProjection/cardDisplayState
constraints: CardExporter.export(scene:skin:) takes CardScene, not a raw Card

decisions.decision: Add a debounced Card.myAnswerDraft field, persisted every ~2s while the Answer sheet is open and cleared on submit/dismiss, to protect a typed-but-unsubmitted answer from being silently lost if the process is killed outright rather than merely backgrounded.
decisions.rationale: Named as the Red Team edge case this round: DEC-detailed_discussion-007 only covers save failures after submit is attempted, not process death before submit is ever attempted, and the Answer sheet is the app's only free-text entry surface.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving typed drafts in local @State only, unprotected against force-quit/memory reclamation
constraints: Debounce write must clear the field on both successful submit and sheet dismiss

decisions.decision: Declare a SchemaV1: VersionedSchema now, even with only one schema version in existence.
decisions.rationale: Costs nothing today and removes a foreseeable later-phase migration scramble when a second schema version is actually needed.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring versioned-schema adoption until an actual second schema version is needed
constraints: makeModelContainer must reference SchemaV1 explicitly

decisions.decision: CoreMotion-derived parallax (GlobeParallax) is held exclusively in GlobeView's own private/ephemeral state, never in AppRouter or any type observed by a SwiftData @Query.
decisions.rationale: Extends design_handoff's CoreMotion/SwiftData-isolation requirement into a concrete, enforceable rule so throttled ~20-30Hz attitude updates can never trigger a full Today-screen re-render, directly protecting against the globe-stutter risk already flagged in next_steps_small.
rejected_alternatives: Piping motion updates through AppRouter or a shared observable object other views also read
constraints: MotionAttitudeService is only ever consumed from within GlobeView's own state, not injected into AppRouter

decisions.decision: Card.dayIndex is a connection-relative integer offset computed by DayBoundary.canonicalDayIndex(for:connectionCreatedAt:) against the UTC calendar, and Prompt selection is prompts[dayIndex % 60] — one integer index unifying the UTC-day-boundary requirement and the 60-day prompt-repeat requirement, replacing a separate date-string dayID.
decisions.rationale: A single integer already accounting for UTC-day-boundary math directly drives both contiguous streak counting and modulo-60 prompt cycling without reconciling two parallel day representations.
rejected_alternatives: Card.dayID as a freeform date string requiring separate modulo logic against a connection-start date elsewhere
constraints: DayBoundary.canonicalDayIndex is the single function that produces this index

decisions.decision: Connection.personThem is a required (non-optional) relationship, since every Connection in this offline build — sample-preview or redeem-code — synthesizes both people locally at creation time; there is no networked pre-join waiting state to model.
decisions.rationale: Removes an impossible-in-this-build nil state from the type system rather than defensively coding around a case that structurally can't occur offline.
rejected_alternatives: Modeling personThem as optional to represent a pre-join waiting state this offline build can never actually produce
constraints: Any future FirebaseSyncService adapter that reintroduces a genuine pre-join gap must revisit this field as optional/async-loaded — explicitly not solved here

decisions.decision: The 'primary connection' (DEC-detailed_discussion-004) is derived at read time from Connection.createdAt (earliest non-sample connection), never stored as a separate primaryOrder or isPrimary field.
decisions.rationale: A stored ordering field is a second source of truth that could drift from actual creation order; deriving it avoids that entirely.
rejected_alternatives: A stored primaryOrder: Int field set at creation time
constraints: EntitlementPolicy.canWrite must compare createdAt across allConnections, not read a cached flag

decisions.decision: Restore the atomic startup/scene-activation reconciliation pass for an interrupted sample-to-real redeem transition as a must-build requirement with its own seeded test, sequenced inside the domain milestone (M1) as a fifth named race alongside the four already locked.
decisions.rationale: This was proposed in tech_specs round 1 by Codex as a real correctness gap but was crowded out of the final DEC-tech_specs-* decision set; without it, a killed process mid-redeem can leave activeConnectionID pointing at a discarded sample connection with no recovery path.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the reconciliation pass as an unimplemented idea from an earlier phase
Treating it as optional polish rather than a correctness invariant
constraints: Must be covered by a fifth seeded race test alongside the four already locked
Cold start and scene-activation must both run the reconciliation check before routing UI

decisions.decision: Bundle persisted-due-date simulated-partner resolution, atomic sample-to-real redeem discard, and the startup reconciliation pass into a single hardened milestone (M1) completed before any UI work begins, rather than spreading them across separate later milestones.
decisions.rationale: All three touch the same Connection/Card lifecycle that every downstream screen (Today, Answer sheet, Timeline) reads as ground truth; if this wobbles, rework is expensive because it's spread across five services rather than contained in one view.
rejected_alternatives: Building these three mechanisms opportunistically as their consuming screens are built
constraints: M1 gate requires all five seeded races green before M2 can start

decisions.decision: Insert an early validation spike for CardScene inside M1 — rendering one CardScene through both a throwaway Canvas view and ImageRenderer and diffing the output — before GlobeView and StaticPNGExporter are built against it as a committed interface.
decisions.rationale: CardScene was adopted last phase on a single contributor's proposal with no adversarial pushback; if its plain CGPoint-array shape doesn't cleanly support real Canvas drawing needs (paths, gradients, blend modes), that mismatch is far cheaper to catch now than during the Compose & Share milestone.
rejected_alternatives: Committing GlobeView and StaticPNGExporter to the CardScene interface without validating it first, discovering any mismatch only when export is wired up late
constraints: Spike must complete inside M1, not deferred to M3 or M5

decisions.decision: Run a headless StoreKit smoke test (fetch products, complete a sandbox purchase, confirm Transaction.currentEntitlements, confirm the .storekit config is attached to the shared scheme) inside the services milestone (M2), well before any Paywall UI exists.
decisions.rationale: The .storekit-config-in-scheme trap is already a named known failure mode; discovering it only in a late Paywall milestone leaves no slack to fix a scheme misconfiguration.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring all StoreKit verification to the Paywall milestone near the end of the build
constraints: Smoke test must run in CI/headless xcodebuild test, not only inside Xcode interactively

decisions.decision: Adopt a concrete globe-rendering performance budget: coastline data capped under 1,500 vertex points, with projected CGPoint paths cached and only recomputed when CoreMotion yaw/pitch crosses a minor threshold.
decisions.rationale: Converts the previously qualitative 'globe must not stutter under parallax' requirement into a concrete, implementable engineering constraint rather than leaving it to be discovered as a performance bug.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the vertex/recompute budget unspecified and tuning reactively if stutter is observed
constraints: Enforced inside M3; verified by manual/smoke check in Simulator with parallax active

decisions.decision: The design-lint script must exist and be runnable from M0 (commit one), scanning an even near-empty tree, rather than being added after screen work has started.
decisions.rationale: An unenforced style promise rots as velocity increases; retrofitting the lint gate after eight screens exist turns it into a cleanup project instead of a running gate, undermining the already-locked automated-lint requirement.
rejected_alternatives: Adding the lint script during the verification milestone (M6) once all screens exist
constraints: Script must be part of M0's deliverables, not M6's

decisions.decision: Connection/Card lifecycle work and CardScene (M1's scope) are assigned to a single owner rather than split across parallel agents; parallel task assignment reopens from M2 onward once the domain contracts are locked and tested.
decisions.rationale: tech_specs itself produced a real type-definition collision (parallel Codable struct vs SwiftData @Model class for the same entities) when two contributors worked this exact area simultaneously; the same risk applies to task assignment for the build phase.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting M1's domain/lifecycle work across multiple parallel agents for speed
constraints: Task assignment phase must not split M1 into parallel lanes covering Connection/Card lifecycle or CardScene

decisions.decision: Verification is distributed per-milestone (each milestone's own risk is tested inside that milestone) rather than end-loaded into one final testing phase; M6 is reserved only for checks that require the whole app to exist.
decisions.rationale: End-loading verification means a late-discovered failure in an early subsystem is maximally expensive to fix; failing fast inside the milestone that created the risk keeps rework local.
rejected_alternatives: A single large verification milestone at the end covering all test types
constraints: M6 is limited to: eight-screen XCUITest crawl, StoreKit-Testing entitlement-lapse scenario, light/dark appearance spot check, Dynamic Type extremes check, full lint run

decisions.decision: Lock the seven-milestone sequence (M0 scaffold/lint, M1 domain+lifecycle hardening, M2 services+StoreKit smoke test, M3 globe performance, M4 router+Today/Answer/Compose, M5 Timeline/Reunion/Settings/Paywall, M6 final verification) at an estimated 16.5–17 engineering days as the synthesis of the three independently proposed plans.
decisions.rationale: Codex's dependency-first structure, Gemini's concrete globe-performance numbers, and Claude's sequencing corrections (restored reconciliation pass, early CardScene spike, earlier StoreKit smoke test, distributed verification) are complementary rather than conflicting; merging them avoids re-litigating milestone order in a later phase.
rejected_alternatives: Adopting Codex's plan unmodified at 13-15 days (omits the reconciliation/spike additions)
Adopting Gemini's plan unmodified at 12 days (too compressed once hardening work is included)
constraints: Task assignment phase should size lanes against this milestone list and day estimate

decisions.decision: Adopt a single Xcode project at Tether/Tether.xcodeproj with one app target and three test targets, using Xcode's file-system-synchronized groups per lane directory so new files auto-join the target without further .pbxproj edits.
decisions.rationale: Four lanes committing concurrently against one .pbxproj is the single biggest structural risk to this phase — not bad Swift, but merge conflicts over target-membership XML; synchronized groups remove that risk almost entirely.
rejected_alternatives: A workspace of multiple sub-projects
Manual .pbxproj edits per lane without synchronized groups, relying on review discipline alone
constraints: The only hand-edit to .pbxproj happens once, in the scaffold task
Every lane's owned directory is its own synchronized group

decisions.decision: data_domain (models, pure domain functions, CardScene, Connection/Card lifecycle hardening) remains single-owner through the M1 gate, per DEC-project_plan-007, and merges into main alone before the other three lanes branch off.
decisions.rationale: tech_specs already produced a real type-definition collision when two contributors worked this exact area in parallel; carrying that lesson into task assignment prevents a repeat during actual implementation.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting Connection/Card lifecycle or CardScene work across parallel data_domain tasks for speed
constraints: T-004 through T-008 (all data_domain M1 tasks) must merge and pass all five seeded races before services_utilities/primary_ui/polish_resilience branches are cut

decisions.decision: TetherApp.swift, the composition root that wires concrete service implementations into the environment, is integrator-owned and not part of any single lane's task backlog; it is edited once at the M2->M4 handoff.
decisions.rationale: Without a single owner, multiple lanes finishing their own service around the same time would race to add their service registration to the same init block, producing avoidable merge conflicts in the one file every lane touches.
rejected_alternatives: Letting each lane's final task include wiring its own service into TetherApp.swift
constraints: No task in the backlog lists TetherApp.swift as an owned file

decisions.decision: Adopt a one-branch-per-lane merge strategy (tether/data-domain, tether/services, tether/primary-ui, tether/polish); data-domain merges first and alone, the other three branch off the updated main afterward and merge independently via PR with no shared integration branch.
decisions.rationale: With synchronized groups removing the structural need for a big-bang merge, there's no reason to force the three downstream lanes through a single integration branch once the domain contracts are locked and tested.
rejected_alternatives: A single shared integration branch all four lanes merge into before anything reaches main
constraints: services_utilities, primary_ui, polish_resilience branches must be cut only after the data_domain M1 gate (five seeded races) is green

decisions.decision: Every task's requirement_ids field is drawn directly from the authoritative DEC-* decisions log rather than from a separately-numbered requirements.json, since the literal requirements.json text produced during app_features was not available verbatim to this phase.
decisions.rationale: Traceability to a real, quotable decision is more valuable than traceability to a placeholder number nobody can verify; the decisions log is the one artifact both this phase and all future phases can actually check tasks against.
rejected_alternatives: Inventing sequential R-0xx placeholder ids not tied to any verifiable source
constraints: A future phase with the literal requirements.json in hand should cross-check this mapping rather than assume it's exhaustive

decisions.decision: Lock a 27-task backlog (T-001 through T-027) across the four fixed lanes, using Claude's scaffold-aware, finer-grained task breakdown as the base rather than Codex's coarser 16-task version.
decisions.rationale: Claude's version resolves a real structural risk (the .pbxproj merge-conflict problem) that Codex's plan didn't address at all; the finer granularity also gives each build worker a smaller, more independently verifiable unit of work.
rejected_alternatives: Using Codex's 16-task version unmodified
Running both task lists in parallel and letting build workers pick
constraints: Every task has exactly one owner_lane, an acyclic dependency graph, and no ownerless task

decisions.decision: Lock seven UI-crawl flows (onboarding+sample-partner-preview, redeem/sample-to-real transition, answer+gated-reveal completion, compose&share with the animated-export paywall trigger, timeline archive, reunion paywall trigger, settings+add-connection paywall trigger), expressed in the tap/type/assert_exists/back primitive schema with explicit accessibilityIdentifiers, replacing Codex's earlier prose-journey format.
decisions.rationale: The UI-crawl gate executes against exact stable identifiers, not free-text journey descriptions; a flow written as prose can't actually be run against the built app.
rejected_alternatives: Keeping Codex's prose-journey flows-json as-is
constraints: primary_ui tasks (T-018 through T-023) must expose every accessibilityIdentifier named in these seven flows on the corresponding control

decisions.decision: services_utilities may never import SwiftUI; any services task that begins importing SwiftUI is a boundary violation to flag during review, not a judgment call.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the I/O-facing service layer cleanly separable from the presentation layer, which is what makes the domain/services split (already locked in ios_architecture_review) actually enforceable rather than aspirational.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing services to import SwiftUI for convenience (e.g. Color-typed skin metadata)
constraints: Code review for services_utilities tasks must check for SwiftUI imports

decisions.decision: Grant a conditional readiness pass: the cross-phase spec is coherent and buildable, contingent on six concrete fixes being folded into the canonical backlog/gate criteria rather than left as implicit decisions-log claims.
decisions.rationale: Thirteen phases of decisions converge cleanly on one narrow app surface with no real contradictions, but several gate-level details in task_assignments would silently produce untestable or under-specified acceptance criteria if build started as-is.
rejected_alternatives: Unconditional pass with no fixes named
Sending the plan back for another full discussion round
constraints: All six fixes below must be applied to their named tasks before those tasks are considered done

decisions.decision: The gated-reveal UI-crawl flow must include an explicit step that advances the simulated partner's due-date/checkpoint before asserting card completion, rather than asserting completion immediately after the user's own answer submission.
decisions.rationale: The persisted-due-date/checkpoint design (DEC-ios_architecture_review-002) means completion is not guaranteed immediately after one side answers; the crawl as drafted would be flaky or falsely pass/fail.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the flow as-is and discovering the flakiness during T-026/T-027 execution
constraints: Applies to the flows-json 'answer + gated-reveal complete' journey and tasks T-026/T-027

decisions.decision: The only canonical task backlog for build is T-001 through T-027 keyed to DEC-* requirement_ids; any earlier R-0XX-keyed draft task list in this project's history is a discarded artifact and must not be used to derive models, tasks, or requirement mappings.
decisions.rationale: Two abandoned draft backlogs using R-0XX ids tied to a requirements.json that never existed are still visible in phase transcripts; a build agent reading raw history instead of the final decision could pick one up and build a second, incompatible domain model set, repeating the exact collision tech_specs already had once.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the dead drafts unlabeled and trusting future readers to infer which list is authoritative
constraints: Any future phase or build agent must treat T-001-T-027 (task_assignments final output) as the sole source of truth for tasks

decisions.decision: T-022's acceptance criteria are extended to require a visible add-connection affordance and a visible primary-vs-read-only indicator per connection within the single flat Settings list.
decisions.rationale: DEC-app_features-002 made add-a-connection must-have specifically so the free-tier downgrade/read-only rule (DEC-prompt_contract-007) is provable; as originally scoped, T-022 could be completed with no way to add a second connection and no visible read-only signal, making the StoreKit lapse test (T-027) unfalsifiable from the UI even if the data-layer test passes.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving T-022's criteria as originally scoped (notification cadence, units, subscription row, sign-out only) and treating the read-only distinction as implied
constraints: Must remain a single flat list per DEC-portfolio_selection-003, no sub-screen

decisions.decision: The bundled .storekit configuration must encode the real product tiers ($4.99/mo, $29.99/yr, 7-day trial) rather than placeholder products.
decisions.rationale: The StoreKit smoke test and entitlement-lapse test are only meaningful if they exercise the actual monetization spec; placeholder SKUs would let the tests pass while proving nothing about the real pricing/trial configuration.
rejected_alternatives: Using placeholder product identifiers and deferring real product configuration to a later phase
constraints: Applies to T-012's .storekit file and its headless smoke test

decisions.decision: The design-lint script must match both the .font(.system(size: modifier form and the Font.system(size: type-initializer form (plus both Color( and UIColor( forms), and a companion check must scan for any third-party SPM dependency and fail the gate if found.
decisions.rationale: The lint pattern as originally specified only named the modifier form, which is a one-character rewrite away from a silent bypass; the no-third-party-package rule (DEC-prompt_contract build constraint) had no mechanical enforcement anywhere in the plan.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on code review alone to catch the type-initializer bypass and stray SPM dependencies
constraints: Applies to T-003's lint_design_system.sh
