decisions.decision: The branch-per-lane/PR merge choreography in task_assignments is reclassified as optional process flavor, not a build requirement; the hard requirement that must be preserved regardless of execution mechanics is the ordering dependency that all data_domain M1 tasks (T-004-T-008) and their five seeded races must be green before services_utilities/primary_ui/polish_resilience work begins.
decisions.rationale: This factory's actual execution pattern is autonomous agent passes writing into one working tree, not a multi-day human team with independent branches and review cycles; literal branch/PR instructions could stall or produce busywork, while the sequencing gate is what actually protects against the tech_specs-style collision risk.
rejected_alternatives: Keeping branch-per-lane as a literal required step regardless of how the build is actually executed
constraints: Whatever executes the build must still enforce the M1-gate-before-downstream-lanes ordering, by whatever mechanism fits the actual execution model

decisions.decision: T-018's acceptance criteria are extended to require the literal button labels and confirmation-sheet copy for 'Preview with a sample partner' vs. 'Redeem a join code' to be written out and sanity-checked against first-time-user misreading risk, not merely asserted as 'copy is explicit.'
decisions.rationale: These two onboarding affordances look similar but have very different consequences (one harmless/reversible, one irreversibly discards sample data and can only ever redeem a self-generated code in this offline build); the existing acceptance criteria had no accountable check that the actual copy achieves the intended clarity.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving copy quality as an unverified implication of 'copy is explicit that...' in the acceptance criteria
constraints: Applies to T-018

decisions.decision: The QA checklist is structured 'state-first': every test step touching a feature the build_verification record already found missing (globe/Canvas/tether, SyncService, Reunion screen, .storekit config, standalone lint script) is explicitly labeled [BLOCKED — feature not built] rather than silently tested, skipped, or graded as tester error.
decisions.rationale: A checklist written against the original prompt rather than against what actually got built would waste QA time hunting for bugs in code that doesn't exist and could produce a false 'app is broken' diagnosis when the real diagnosis is 'app was never finished' — these require completely different follow-up actions.
rejected_alternatives: Writing a generic checklist against the original prompt with no acknowledgment of build_verification's findings
Silently skipping untestable steps with no note in the final report
constraints: Any future QA pass on this app must re-check whether each [BLOCKED] item has since been built before treating it as still blocked

decisions.decision: Missing Reunion screen is graded as a hard fail against a locked must-have requirement (DEC-app_features-003), not filed as a 'known limitation.'
decisions.rationale: Reunion-the-screen-plus-paywall-gating was explicitly locked must-have, never downgraded anywhere in the decision log; treating its absence as an acceptable limitation would misrepresent an unmet hard requirement as a scoped-out one.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Reunion's absence as an accepted limitation alongside genuinely accepted ones (e.g. backgrounded-heartbeat)
constraints: Final review must carry this forward as an unmet must-have, not a soft gap

decisions.decision: Confirming that xcodebuild test (not just xcodebuild build) actually executed the 47-method TetherTests suite is a blocking prerequisite before anyone treats that suite as a passing gate.
decisions.rationale: build_verification explicitly flagged this was never independently confirmed in this project; a QA process that inherits that gap silently would let 'compiled cleanly' get conflated with 'tests passed' a second time.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming the test suite passed because it was 'wired in correctly' per write_tests' hand-verification
constraints: This check must happen before final sign-off on this app

decisions.decision: The onboarding QA script requires recording the literal button labels and sheet copy for 'Preview with a sample partner' vs. 'Redeem a join code,' and flags a failure if neither clearly signals the redeem action's irreversible, data-discarding consequence.
decisions.rationale: These two actions look similar but have very different consequences (one harmless/reversible, one irreversible); implementation_readiness_gate already required this copy be written out and sanity-checked (T-018), and this is the first point in the project that actually exercises that requirement against the built app rather than trusting it was done.
rejected_alternatives: Treating copy clarity as implied/passed without an explicit tester check
constraints: Applies to the onboarding section of this checklist

decisions.decision: The StoreKit entitlement-lapse test requires actively attempting a write (answering a card) on a read-only, non-primary connection and confirming it is rejected, not just confirming the UI shows a read-only indicator.
decisions.rationale: DEC-ios_architecture_review-017 requires entitlement-gated writes be rejected from a single domain policy point, not merely hidden via UI visibility; a QA pass that only checks the visible indicator would not actually verify the underlying no-data-loss guarantee.
rejected_alternatives: Treating a visible read-only badge as sufficient evidence the rule is enforced
constraints: Applies to the Settings/Connections section of this checklist

decisions.decision: Offline/Airplane Mode testing is scoped to a negative check (behavior must be identical to normal launch) rather than a positive feature test, since this is a fully local app with no network dependency to exercise.
decisions.rationale: The app has no real network calls in this build; the meaningful offline test is confirming nothing unexpectedly tries to hit a network path, not verifying degraded-but-functional offline behavior as in a networked app.
rejected_alternatives: Writing offline-mode test steps as if the app had real network-dependent features to degrade gracefully
constraints: Applies to the offline-behavior section of this checklist

decisions.decision: Tether is graded NOT launch-ready and must not be submitted to App Store review in its current state.
decisions.rationale: The paid tier (Reunion, animated export) sells features that don't exist on disk, the free tier's signature hero visual (globe/tether) is two placeholder circles, and no .storekit configuration exists to even exercise the purchase flow — this is a functional-completeness and trust risk, not a cosmetic one.
rejected_alternatives: Submitting with marketing copy written against the intended vision rather than the built app
Treating this as launch-ready with cosmetic caveats
constraints: No public App Store metadata, screenshots, or submission should proceed until the blockers below are resolved or explicitly scoped out

decisions.decision: The intended one-sentence App Store promise and neutral audience framing are locked now for future use, but all screenshot/storyboard production is blocked until the app actually renders the depicted UI.
decisions.rationale: Apple rejects listings whose screenshots don't reflect real running behavior (Guideline 2.3.3); writing copy/screenshots against the vision rather than the build would be fiction and a rejection risk.
rejected_alternatives: Producing screenshots now against mocked or design-spec renders instead of the real app
constraints: Promise copy must keep 'your person' neutral language, never default to 'partner'
The seven-shot storyboard plan (onboarding, hero card, answer sheet, compose&share, timeline, reunion, paywall) is preserved as a plan but marked not-ready

decisions.decision: The honest Apple privacy nutrition label for this local-first build is 'Data Not Collected' — no location, photos, contacts, analytics, or ad-network data leaves the device, since there is no network layer at all.
decisions.rationale: City-level home location is picked from a bundled list and stored purely locally with nothing to transmit it anywhere; this is a real, defensible, and appealing privacy claim as long as it stays true to the current architecture.
rejected_alternatives: Pre-emptively labeling for the future Firebase adapter's data model
constraints: This label must be revisited and rewritten the day a real cloud sync adapter ships (linked identity, connection data, push tokens) — that revision is a required task for whoever builds that adapter, not an afterthought

decisions.decision: No permission prompts (location, notifications, photos) are requested anywhere in this build, and the only permission-adjacent copy needed is the Settings notification-cadence control, which must explicitly state it governs foreground/in-app alerts only.
decisions.rationale: There is structurally nothing to push in a fully offline, foreground-only build; implying background delivery would be a dishonest affordance.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting notification permission preemptively for a future cloud adapter
constraints: Settings copy must state this scoping explicitly, extending the already-locked DEC-detailed_discussion-010/DEC-ios_architecture_review-007 requirements

decisions.decision: Four concrete subscription/paywall review risks are named as release blockers: animated export permanently 'coming soon' for paying subscribers (Guideline 2.1 risk), Reunion missing entirely despite being a paid paywall trigger, no .storekit config existing to exercise purchase/restore/cancellation, and standard subscription disclosure copy (price/duration, auto-renewal language, Terms/Privacy links, Restore Purchases) not yet written/reviewed.
decisions.rationale: Selling a subscription tier whose flagship features don't exist is both an App Review rejection risk and a real user-trust risk if it somehow passed review; these are functional gaps, not copy nitpicks.
rejected_alternatives: Treating these as minor polish items to fix post-submission
constraints: None of these four may be waved through as 'fix later' before any submission attempt

decisions.decision: A live privacy-policy URL and a monitored support email/URL are required App Store Connect metadata that must exist before submission, independent of any code-level blockers.
decisions.rationale: This is mandatory subscription-app metadata that nobody in this project had named yet; it's a logistics task, not a build task, but it blocks submission just as hard as the code gaps.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring support/legal setup until code blockers are resolved, treating it as lower priority
constraints: Must be set up as an explicit, ownable task separate from the build backlog

decisions.decision: Two honest paths forward are offered for closing the gap: fully finish the real blockers (hero card, real SyncService pairing, Reunion, working .storekit config, actual DesignSystem tokens), or cut scope hard and ship a free-tier-only app with Reunion and animated export pulled from both the paywall and all marketing copy as a fast-follow.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with the standing rule to prefer a smaller finished app over a larger half-built one; submitting today's build with today's paywall is the one combination that risks a real complaint, not just a review rejection.
rejected_alternatives: Submitting the current build with the current paywall and marketing copy unchanged
constraints: Whichever path is chosen, no paywall trigger may advertise an entitlement the app cannot currently deliver

decisions.decision: Tether receives a final verdict of NO-GO: the app is not complete against its own locked contract and is not ready to be treated as done or shipped.
decisions.rationale: The app's central hero surface (globe, tether, live distance, dual clock) does not exist, SyncService/Reunion/.storekit/DesignSystem tokens are all missing against locked must-haves, and the authoritative build now reports a test failure on top of the missing features.
rejected_alternatives: Grading this a conditional pass on the strength of the compiling domain layer
Treating the test failure as a minor footnote given prior hand-verification claims
constraints: No downstream phase or user-facing claim should describe this build as feature-complete or launch-ready

decisions.decision: Identifying and root-causing the newly-surfaced test failure (compiled cleanly + TESTS FAILED) is the mandatory first follow-up, ahead of any new feature work.
decisions.rationale: This project's manual hand-verification track record has now missed two real compile bugs and failed to predict this test failure; no claim about the domain layer's correctness (including the gated-reveal state machine, the app's one designated correctness invariant) can be trusted until the actual failing tests are read directly.
rejected_alternatives: Proceeding with new feature work (globe, SyncService, Reunion) while the test failure remains uninvestigated
Continuing to rely on hand-traced 'no breakage' claims as sufficient verification
constraints: Any future phase must report which specific tests failed and why before claiming the domain/test layer is solid

decisions.decision: app_store_readiness's 'do not submit' verdict is reaffirmed and treated as reinforced, not reopened, by this phase's findings.
decisions.rationale: The missing-feature list (globe/tether, SyncService, Reunion, .storekit, DesignSystem tokens) that justified the earlier do-not-submit call is unchanged, and the new test failure adds an additional reason rather than any reason to reconsider.
rejected_alternatives: Treating final_review as a fresh, independent readiness assessment that could reach a different launch conclusion
constraints: Any future submission attempt must resolve both the app_store_readiness blockers and the test failure named here

decisions.decision: The two-path fork from app_store_readiness (finish the real blockers vs. cut hard to a smaller free-tier-only release) remains explicitly unresolved and is handed off as a scoping decision for whoever resumes work, not decided by this phase.
decisions.rationale: All three contributors this round named the same follow-ups but none picked a path; forcing a choice without a resourcing/timeline owner present would be arbitrary.
rejected_alternatives: This phase unilaterally choosing 'finish' or 'cut' on the group's behalf
constraints: Whoever resumes this project must make this choice explicitly before further UI/feature work proceeds

decisions.decision: Portfolio audit is marked not applicable for Tether — this is a confirmed single-app run with one project folder, one Xcode project/target, and no sibling apps or children.
decisions.rationale: portfolio_selection already locked this as a single app with no category split requested in the original prompt; task_assignments and build_coordination confirm exactly one project folder exists with no portfolio manifest ever produced.
rejected_alternatives: Inventing portfolio-shape work or a manifest audit where none was ever requested or produced
constraints: Expected app count = 1 (tether); no child folder/workflow checks apply

decisions.decision: This phase's 'not applicable / no issues' result must not be interpreted downstream as project readiness — it certifies folder/project shape only, and final_review's NO-GO verdict on functional completeness stands unchanged.
decisions.rationale: portfolio_audit and final_review answer different questions (shape vs. completeness); running portfolio_audit after a NO-GO final_review creates a risk that a later automated step could misread this phase's clean pass as an all-clear signal.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving this distinction implicit and letting downstream tooling infer it
constraints: Any Jira/Notion backfill from this phase must carry final_review's NO-GO status forward, not a standalone 'portfolio audit passed' status

decisions.decision: Fix scope is exactly the design-lint gate: resolve every error entry in a freshly regenerated docs/design_lint.json, starting from the one currently-known hard error (self-referential raw_font_size match inside ResilienceHelpers.swift's own lint-detection helper at line 69), not a broader app change.
decisions.rationale: Codex confirmed only one hard error currently exists; Claude's caveat that the JSON (not the prompt's 'e.g.' example) is the authoritative list is a condition on the same scope, not a competing scope.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the single named example in the prompt as the complete fix target
Expanding scope to any other subsystem
constraints: Must re-run the lint script fresh (not reuse stale docs/design_lint.json) before declaring done
Diff limited to files the fresh lint output actually names

decisions.decision: The ResilienceHelpers.swift:69 false positive is fixed by restructuring the probe-string construction inside containsInlineFontOrColor(_:) (e.g. building the search token from concatenated pieces) so the helper's own source no longer self-matches, without reducing its detection coverage of real violations elsewhere.
decisions.rationale: The helper's own source literally contains the raw-font-size pattern it searches for in other files, causing a self-referential false positive; the fix must remove the self-match without weakening the check.
rejected_alternatives: Adding a blanket exemption for ResilienceHelpers.swift or lint-helper files in general beyond what's already exempted
Softening the regex/pattern match to stop catching this case at the cost of catching fewer real violations
constraints: No new per-file exemption added to the lint script
Lint script must still flag inline font/color usage in all non-exempt files after the change

decisions.decision: Before patching ResilienceHelpers.swift, confirm it is live, referenced code; if it is unreferenced dead scaffold, deletion is the preferred minimal fix over patching it to be lint-clean.
decisions.rationale: The file doesn't correspond to any named component in the locked architecture (Theme.swift, GlobeView, CardScene, SyncService, EntitlementStore), raising the possibility it's orphaned scaffold from an earlier lane.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming the file is live and patching without checking references
constraints: Verify at least one real call site/reference exists before treating patch-in-place as the answer

decisions.decision: Any additional real design-lint violations found in the freshly regenerated JSON are fixed by substituting an existing DesignSystem/Theme type-ramp token (display/title/headline/body/caption/meta); a new token is added only if nothing in the existing ramp fits, and must be a single narrow addition.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the fix consistent with the already-locked single-source-of-truth type ramp rather than inventing per-callsite styling.
rejected_alternatives: Inlining a fixed point size directly to silence the lint without going through the token system
constraints: No ramp redesign; additions must be minimal and justified by an unmet use case

decisions.decision: This phase's fix is scoped strictly away from Connection/Card lifecycle, SyncService, globe rendering, StoreKit, and Reunion, and passing the lint gate does not change or imply anything about the app's overall NO-GO status from final_review.
decisions.rationale: Those are separate, already-tracked, much larger gaps with no mandate opened by this narrow gate-fix request; conflating 'lint passes' with 'app is done' would misrepresent status given this project's history of overclaiming completeness.
rejected_alternatives: Treating a passing lint gate as evidence the app is closer to launch-ready
constraints: No downstream claim may describe this fix as resolving final_review's NO-GO verdict

decisions.decision: The design-lint gate fix requested for this iteration is confirmed closed: xcodebuild reports a clean compile for the iOS Simulator, and no inline Color(/UIColor(/raw font-size violations remain outside DesignSystem.swift, with no new third-party dependency introduced.
decisions.rationale: This is the first phase in the project's history with an actual compiler-confirmed (not hand-verified) build result, directly satisfying the phase's acceptance criteria for the lint gate.
rejected_alternatives: Treating hand-verification alone as sufficient, as prior rounds had to
constraints: xcodebuild test still needs to be run and confirmed passing before the test suite (including the gated-reveal state machine) can be trusted as correct, not just compiling

decisions.decision: Tether's overall status remains NO-GO; the app is not ready to submit or be treated as feature-complete against its own locked contract.
decisions.rationale: The two highest-impact locked must-haves — the native globe/tether Canvas hero visual and a working .storekit configuration for the now-fully-wired purchase flow — are both still missing, and xcodebuild test has not been confirmed to pass.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the successful compile and the real Reunion/onboarding/streak work as sufficient to move to a conditional-go or go verdict
constraints: No downstream claim may describe this app as launch-ready or feature-complete until the globe/tether visual exists, a real .storekit config is attached to the scheme, and xcodebuild test is confirmed passing

decisions.decision: The process record is corrected: despite being chartered as a narrow lint-only fix walled off from Connection/Card lifecycle, SyncService, globe rendering, StoreKit, and Reunion, the actual four-iteration build_coordination arc substantially built out all of those areas (Today hero screen, full Reunion screen, PairingService/PaywallGate/NotificationScheduler, EntitlementService wiring, StoreKit gating, streak algorithm rewrite).
decisions.rationale: The prior phase's decisions log claims a diff 'limited to files the fresh lint output names,' which is factually false against what was actually built; letting that framing stand uncorrected would misrepresent this project's process discipline to future phases.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the narrow-scope framing unchallenged since the resulting functional progress was net positive
constraints: Future 'small scoped fix' requests in this project should not be assumed to stay scoped just because they are labeled that way; scope adherence should be independently checked against the actual diff, not the stated intent

decisions.decision: The requested design-lint gate fix is confirmed closed and compiler-verified: xcodebuild build compiles cleanly for the iOS Simulator (after one repair for an unrelated read-only accessibilityReduceMotion environment-key bug), and a fresh full-tree sweep shows zero hits on all four forbidden design-lint tokens outside DesignSystem.swift, with no new third-party dependency introduced.
decisions.rationale: This is the narrow scope this iteration was chartered to fix, and it is now backed by an actual compiler-confirmed build result rather than hand-verification alone.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the build failure at the start of this arc as evidence the lint fix itself was incomplete
constraints: No downstream claim may describe this as evidence the app overall is closer to launch-ready than final_review-1 found

decisions.decision: Tether's overall status remains NO-GO, reaffirming rather than reopening final_review-1's verdict, despite substantial real progress this build arc (working pairing loop, native globe/tether hero visual now wired into the build).
decisions.rationale: Two independent council members converged on the same blocking reasons: xcodebuild test has never been confirmed to actually run and pass (only xcodebuild build was verified this round), and the Tether+ paywall still sells at least two undelivered features (animated export, Year Tethered retrospective reel) plus one unenforced entitlement (the free-tier one-connection cap, since canCreateAdditionalConnection() is hardcoded true) -- a hard App Store/user-trust blocker that predates and survives this round unchanged.
rejected_alternatives: Grading this a conditional-go or go verdict on the strength of the compiling build and the newly-real pairing/globe work
Scoping final_review narrowly to only the lint-fix objective and staying silent on overall app readiness
constraints: No downstream claim may describe this app as launch-ready or feature-complete until xcodebuild test is confirmed passing (including the gated-reveal state machine), animated export + Year Tethered reel are either built or removed from the paywall/marketing copy, and canCreateAdditionalConnection() is routed through EntitlementPolicy

decisions.decision: The pairing loop (AppRouter.redeemJoinCode/hydrate/onSceneBecameActive wired to real LocalSyncService calls, sample-to-real transition creating a fresh Connection instead of mutating in place) and the native globe/tether Canvas hero visual (wired into Today and Timeline, present in the Xcode project) are recognized as genuine, substantive progress against final_review-1's two biggest named gaps.
decisions.rationale: These were the two most-repeated blockers across four prior build_coordination iterations; both are now real, wired, and part of the compiling build, not placeholder or unreferenced code.
rejected_alternatives: Treating this progress as immaterial because the app overall remains NO-GO
constraints: This progress must be stated plainly in any future status summary, not buried under the NO-GO headline
